title: The Third Street theatre
body: The theatre on Third Street is worth the trip. Three thousand people pass through it every month, and nothing about it feels thin or cheap. I thanked the usher, found my seat, and thought through the plot. By the third act my throat was dry and my thumb ached. On the path north I counted thirty thistles, took a deep breath, and thought about the truth of it. Both of us needed this. That is something worth thinking about.

title: They gathered there
body: They gathered there with their mother and father rather than wait for better weather. This was the other brother, the one they had not seen. Neither of them said anything, though they smiled. Then they breathed together, smoothed the clothes on the bench, and moved farther in. Whether these were the same people they remembered, or those they had invented, mattered less than the fact that they were all there, and that they had come without being asked.

title: The village above the river
body: Every visitor believes the village above the river is very beautiful. Seven boats leave the bay at eleven, and the brave ones vote to move over to the far bank. I have never valued a view above this one. My brother bought a van, drove it over the bridge, and never came back before eleven. Believe me: the vase on the table by the bay window is worth more than the boat, but I would rather have the boat.

title: The zoo on Tuesday
body: His cousins chose the zoo because the zebras were easy to see. Zero prizes, no music, just thousands of noses pressed against the glass. The roses by the houses were freezing, and the bees were buzzing anyway. Please close your eyes, she says, and choose. Those days always surprise us: the sun rises, the birds sing, the buses arrive, and nobody is busy. It is a small thing, but it is ours, and it is enough.

title: A pleasure to measure
body: It was a pleasure to measure the treasure she found in the garage. The television showed a vision of the ocean: ships, shells, and a shining shore. Her decision was casual, almost unusual — she should share it, she said, but she was not sure. The usual pressure of a short shift makes the machine crash. In the shade of the beige shed we washed the dishes, finished the fish, and watched the sunshine wash across the shallow beach.

title: The ship and the sheep
body: The ship left the beach at six, and the sheep did not sing. It is easy to fill a field and easy to feel it fill. His fist hit the seat and his feet slipped. Did she leave, or did she live here still? The green bin is big, the bean is thin, and this cheese is his. Please pick it, peel it, sit still, and see. Between the ridge and the reach, the difference is one little thing.

title: The cat and the cup
body: The cat sat on the mat, and the cut on my hand hurt. My aunt had a bad hat and a rough cup of coffee. Half the family ran back, laughed, and grabbed the last bag. Some of us understood the trouble: a cap is not a cup, and a match is not much. That sad man had had enough. He stood up, brushed the ash off his jacket, and came back happy, hungry, and calm.

title: Spring Street school
body: The student stopped at the school on Spring Street to study Spanish. He speaks slowly, stands straight, and still struggles with strange scripts. The station screen showed a small storm spreading across the state. Sport, stress, and sleep: three things he could not square. He scratched a sketch on the screen, smiled, and started again. Speaking is a skill, he said, and skills stay strong only if you stop starting over and simply keep speaking.

title: The young singer
body: The young singer was singing a long song all morning. Nothing was wrong: the ring on her finger, the strong tongue of the bell, the thing among the things. Bringing a single English sentence to an ending takes practice. Hang on, keep going, and stop thinking about winning. In the evening she was still walking and talking, humming something, banging on the railing, and everything she was learning was hanging on one sound.

title: The rural library
body: The rural library really rewards a regular reader. Roll the words around: red, yellow, orange, purple. Her right arm was rarely relaxed, and her real problem was the letter L. Collect the flowers, follow the trail, and pull the little cart along the low wall. Rain fell all around the world, and the girl laughed, ran, and let it fall. Correct or wrong, right or left, she rolled her wheel and travelled on.

title: In June the judge
body: In June the judge took a huge journey across the yellow bridge. Yes, you are young, he joked, but your language is your job. Just yesterday a giant orange jacket jumped out at us in the village. Use your usual judgement: the danger is not the jungle beyond the year, it is the year itself. A million opinions, a general jumble, and yet a gentle page — the majority of us usually manage.

title: She asked for the texts
body: She asked for the texts, checked the lists, and finished the tasks. The guests walked in, laughed, and wanted the facts. Six months passed; the worlds she had watched changed, and the tests she had failed turned into tests she passed. He jumped, stopped, and picked up the boxes he had dropped. Twelve desks, three drafts, and a thousand acts later, nothing looked the same. She smiled, thanked them, and left the room exactly as she had found it.
